title: World Bank Taps Circle and Citi to Test Stablecoins for Development Payments
detail:
World Bank Taps Circle and Citi to Test Stablecoins for Development Payments
Decrypt Staff
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 2:56 PM CST 2 min read
CRCL
C
USDC-USD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The World Bank is turning to stablecoins to modernize how it moves development money, announcing Tuesday it will explore using Circle's USDC and blockchain-based payment rails to speed up and cut the cost of disbursing funds around the world.

The institution said it will work with Citi and Circle to test how dollar-denominated, regulated stablecoins could operate alongside or improve its existing funds-distribution system, which runs on correspondent banking, the slow and costly network of intermediary banks that routes international payments.

Under the arrangement, Citi would supply its connections to established banking rails while Circle provides the infrastructure to mint and settle funds in USDC.

The logic is that even small efficiency gains, applied across the vast sums the World Bank moves, could free up meaningful resources for development. "This initiative is about exploring ways to make the financial plumbing of development work better for the people who need it most," said World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, arguing that faster, cheaper money movement means "a health clinic gets built on time, a farmer gets paid before the harvest season ends."

The effort builds on FundsChain, a World Bank blockchain platform designed to make fund disbursements more traceable. More than 350 projects across 96 countries are already onboarded to its digital ledgers, letting everyone involved in a project see how money is being spent.

The stablecoin exploration would focus initially on an intermediated, interoperable model, limited to borrower countries where digital assets are permitted, with plans to involve other banks over time.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire framed development finance as one of the most important applications for his company's technology, saying money that moves "at the speed of the internet shouldn't be reserved for the world's biggest banks and corporations."

Citi's Shahmir Khaliq said the collaboration would deliver "24/7 capabilities at scale so that critical funds move in real time."

The move hands the stablecoin industry a powerful institutional validator, and it fits a broader wave of traditional finance embracing the technology.

How Wall Street Is Racing to Claim the Onchain Dollar

Wall Street is currently racing to claim the onchain dollar, with Goldman Sachs, Citi and other banks committing roughly $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture, while Deutsche Bank recently went live with crypto custody after a five-year buildout.

For Circle, whose USDC is the second-largest stablecoin, a role in the World Bank's payment plumbing marks a notable step toward mainstream legitimacy, even as the broader crypto market endures a rough stretch of ETF outflows and falling prices.

title: Citi Rules Out Major Wealth Acquisitions in Hunt for $5T
detail:
Citi Rules Out Major Wealth Acquisitions in Hunt for $5T
Denise Wee
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:52 AM CST 3 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Copyright Oli Scarff, Getty Images

You can find original article here WealthManagement. Subscribe to our free daily WealthManagement newsletters.

(Bloomberg) -- Citigroup Inc. is pursuing $5 trillion in wealth balances held by existing clients with rival firms, while ruling out major acquisitions, according to its wealth chief.

"We're focused on organic growth," Andy Sieg said in an interview in Shanghai. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser has been "extremely clear" over the past six months that the bank's strategy centers "exclusively on organic growth," he said.

Sieg's remarks follow a report that Citigroup's top executives were weighing the purchase of a major regional bank to bolster deposits. The New York-based lender oversees about $1.4 trillion in client balances, leaving its wealth division trailing Wall Street peers such as Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase & Co.

"We always think about different options," Sieg said. "But we've just simplified the business dramatically over the last five years, and we feel like the footprint that we have today and the booking centers that we have today are the right ones for us."

Fraser has spent the past several years streamlining the lender by cutting thousands of jobs and exiting international consumer businesses. The turnaround is gaining traction, with Citigroup recently posting its strongest third quarter in a decade. Sieg joined from Bank of America Corp. in 2023 to overhaul the wealth unit—a central pillar of Fraser's push to lift returns.

In the third quarter, the bank attracted a record $38 billion of net new investment assets globally. Sieg expects to continue delivering high single-digit organic growth in new flows.

To grow assets, the bank is looking to leverage off its investment bank, having introduced "partnership awards" to encourage collaboration between the investment bank and wealth. They were paid out for the first time this year.

It's also using its retail footprint in the US, Hong Kong and Singapore to deepen relationships with its affluent clients, said Sieg.

The Asia Pacific wealth business generated revenue of $2.58 billion in the first nine months of the year, up 13% from a year ago. It's one of the fastest growing regions for the bank, said Sieg. It makes up about 27% of overall wealth revenue.

"We're going to maintain discipline, but you're going to see steady growth in our banker headcount continuing in Asia," said Sieg.

Sieg, who spent last week traveling across cities in China, including Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen, said that technological innovation in the world's second largest economy is fueling wealth creation and growth.

title: Hong Kong, Swift and Major Banks Test Blockchain-Based Cross-Border Payments
detail:
Hong Kong, Swift and Major Banks Test Blockchain-Based Cross-Border Payments
Amin Haqshanas
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 9:49 AM CST 2 min read
HSBC
601988.SS
HSBC
LINK
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Hong Kong's central bank and Swift are working with major banks to test cross-border payments using tokenized deposits.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said Monday that HSBC Holdings (NYSE: $HSBC), Standard Chartered (LSE: STAN) and Bank of China (HKEX: 3988) are taking part in the initiative, which will connect Swift's blockchain-based ledger with Project Ensemble, Hong Kong's platform for settling tokenized assets and deposits.

The experiment aims to make international payments possible around the clock, including outside traditional banking hours.

More From Cryptoprowl:

NYSE Parent ICE to Bring Hyperliquid-Based Perpetual Futures to US

Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Price Forecast To $1.6 Million By 2036

Survey Finds 90% Of Large Businesses Are Embracing Tokenized Money

Moody's Assigns Investment-Grade Rating To Ripple's Stablecoin

Stablecoin Firm RedotPay To Hold IPO By Year's End: Reports

The project builds on cooperation that began in 2023, when the HKMA and Swift started examining ways to connect central bank digital currency (CBDC) systems. It also follows a November 2 upgrade to Project Ensemble's pilot phase, which introduced 24/7 settlement of tokenized deposit transactions using tokenized central bank money.

"This collaboration represents another significant step in exploring how tokenised deposits and interoperable infrastructure can support real-time, always-on and programmable cross-border transactions," Howard Lee, deputy chief executive of the HKMA, said.

Swift has also been expanding its blockchain infrastructure. In September, the organization tapped Chainlink (CRYPTO: $LINK) to develop infrastructure that will allow banks to connect their internal systems and transaction-signing processes directly to Swift's blockchain-based ledger.

The Hong Kong initiative comes as other major banks move beyond testing. On Monday, JPMorgan (NYSE: $JPM) and Singapore's DBS (SGX: D05) announced that they had connected their blockchain deposit networks, allowing approved clients to transfer tokenized US dollars between the two countries around the clock.

In September, DBS and Citi (NYSE: $C) also completed what they claimed to be the first weekend US dollar payment between Singapore and the US using tokenized deposits.

title: Could Citigroup Actually Climb 30%? Or Is HSBC Totally Wrong?
detail:
Could Citigroup Actually Climb 30%? Or Is HSBC Totally Wrong?
Wiltone Asuncion
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:46 AM CST 4 min read
C
HSBC

Trading disclosure
Could Citigroup Actually Climb 30%? Or Is HSBC Totally Wrong? ©@Gang Zhou from Getty Images via Canva, @Vertigo3d from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

HSBC kept its Buy rating on Citigroup on Nov. 12 and cut its price target to $158 from $164, still 30% above the Nov. 16 close.

Analysts have raised their 2026 and 2027 earnings estimates for Citigroup over the past three months, and TIKR's consensus now sits at $11.40 a share for 2026 and $13.06 for 2027.

HSBC's target implies about 1.6x today's tangible book value, above the 1.47x peak Citigroup hit in June, its highest in five years.

Citigroup can likely earn its way to $158 as tangible book grows, but probably not within twelve months. Its fourth-quarter report and 2027 outlook on Jan. 14 are the next test.

Citigroup (C:NYSE) is 17% below its June closing high, even after posting its best third-quarter revenue in a decade. On Nov. 12, HSBC kept its Buy rating on Citi and set a $158 price target, down from $164 but still 30% above the Nov. 16 close of $121.32.

A strong quarter, with a softer finish ahead

In Citi's third quarter, reported Oct. 13, revenue rose 8% to $23.8 billion, earnings per share rose to $2.85 from $1.86, and Services grew revenue 15% at a 31.2% return on tangible common equity (RoTCE). CEO Jane Fraser said Citi expects "to exceed this year's return target, even as we pull forward investments toward our 11-13% near-term goal."

Returns did slip, though. Firmwide RoTCE fell to 11.5% from 13% in the second quarter. CFO Gonzalo Luchetti said fourth-quarter RoTCE should land "at a high single-digit rate," with Markets revenue expected to fall about 20% from the third quarter, possibly a bit more.

TIKR tracks 23 analysts on Citigroup. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Citigroup, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Citigroup's Analyst Ratings

Does 1.6x tangible book add up?

HSBC's $158 target sits 5% above the $151 mean target of the 21 analysts with published targets, and the Street's highest target is $170.

The consensus target rose from $114 a year ago to a peak of $156 in mid-July. It has eased to $151 since:

Citigroup (C): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

Earnings estimates are still rising. TIKR's consensus calls for normalized EPS of $11.40 for 2026 and $13.06 for 2027. On Yahoo Finance's tally, the 2026 estimate has risen to $11.19 from $10.91 three months ago, and 2027's to $12.95 from $12.62:

Citigroup (C): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

The multiple is the harder part. Citi trades at 1.22x tangible book value, well above its five-year average of 0.81x:

Citigroup (C): price/tangible book value, last 5 years (TIKR)

HSBC's target works out to about 1.6x Citi's tangible book value per share. That's above the 1.47x peak of June 22, the highest of the last five years. Tangible book rose 6% in the year to Sept. 30, to $101.59 a share, and analysts expect $122.01 by the end of 2028. On that book, $158 would be about 1.3x, inside the range Citi has traded at this year.

Long positioning of $45.9 billion has an average entry level of 7,768, against a prevailing market level of 7,573. That leaves 95% of positions underwater, the team led by David Chew said in a positioning note.

A further failure to retain the index's recent 2.5% rebound "raises the spectre of long liquidation that could amplify downside momentum," the strategists wrote.

The recent improvement in U.S. positioning came mainly from short covering rather than new long buying, Citi noted. "Much of the improvement was driven by short covering rather than new long accumulation, indicating investors are reducing bearish exposure rather than expressing a stronger bullish view," the strategists said.

Nasdaq positioning has returned to neutral, while Russell 2000 positioning remains one of the most extended bearish exposures globally.

Russell shorts are largely in profit, leaving them vulnerable to a squeeze, the strategists said. The open question is whether a catalyst exists, such as a dovish shift in Federal Reserve expectations or softer-than-expected inflation data.

Europe was the only region showing broad-based new long accumulation. The Euro Stoxx 50 drew $4.9 billion in new risk flows with no short covering, which the analysts called conviction buying. The DAX and FTSE also strengthened.

Short positions across European indexes are all offside. The Euro Stoxx has the largest at $7.3 billion, with an average entry of 6,155 against a current level of 6,397.

European banks combine elevated short exposure, at the 94th percentile, with rising squeeze risk. Their shorts are 3.4% offside, meaning further improvement in sentiment could trigger a sharp covering cycle, the analysts said.

Elsewhere, Asia positioning risks center on profitable shorts. The strategists said Nikkei and China A50 carry the greatest flow risk, since large short positions there are in profit. That creates scope for profit-taking and faster covering if sentiment improves.

Last week's sticky inflation print set a more hawkish backdrop, they added.
